newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet following last week's heavy volume at prices $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt higher than the previous week, feedlot sources said. There were no reported bids early Monday, with cattle owners asking $69.00 to $70.00.
"I would think with all the cattle they (packers) bought last week, we won't see them be back until Wednesday," one Panhandle cattle feeder said.
The bulk of cattle in the Panhandle area and Kansas last week sold at $69.00, although there were a few light sales late at $68.00. Nebraska cattlemen reported a top of $70.00.
Fed cattle prices this week were seen steady with last week's late sales of $68.00 unless beef prices can maintain strength from last week, sources said.
Beef values last week were buoyed by strong retail demand, but talk circulated that demand for the month had peaked.
Beef movement last week totalled 973 fabricated loads, well below 1,629 the previous week, which was the second highest of the year, according to USDA statistics.
The statistics also showed a $4.59 per cwt increase in heavyweight choice beef last week.
However, prices on Friday for the heavier-weight choice beef slipped $0.22, the first decline since April 9, which fueled concern prices had topped, sources said.
